title: Parabolic Anderson model on the Sierpiński gasket
page_description: Interactive level-8 simulation of the Itô parabolic Anderson model on the Sierpiński gasket with space-time white noise and point-mass initial data.
model_caption: One realization of the Itô parabolic Anderson model with Neumann boundary conditions. Space–time white noise is defined relative to dt μ(dx), where μ is the normalized Hausdorff measure on the gasket. The initial condition places one unit of mass at x₀.
reading_caption: Height and color show u(t,x), with scales adjusted at each time to reveal local peaks. Peak / mean compares the spatial maximum with ∫u dμ. This realization illustrates spatial concentration; it does not estimate the ensemble moment growth that defines intermittency.
numerical_accuracy_note: Time-step sensitivity: comparing Δt with 2Δt gives a 22.4% relative weighted L² difference at the final time, or 4.1% after normalizing each profile by its total mass. The normalized difference reaches 15.9% over saved times. This path is a qualitative illustration; absolute amplitudes and individual peak locations remain sensitive to time resolution.
method_note: The initial peak comes from the point-mass initial condition. Later peaks should be interpreted separately from that initial concentration. In log view, values below one millionth of the current spatial maximum share the lowest color; numerical values remain unchanged.
equation_accessible_text: The time derivative of u equals kappa times the Neumann gasket Laplacian of u plus lambda times u times space-time white noise.
